messages:
Jordan (Docs): Heads-up: linkcheck started failing after the site build. Broken fragment /guides/upgrade#sidebar-collapse mentioned in the log
DocBot: docs-ci | ERROR: Broken fragment -> /guides/upgrade#sidebar-collapse (404)
Jordan (Docs): The guide's H2 is `## Sidebar collapse: when codefence breaks` and there's a fenced code block right before it. Think the markdown -> HTML transform moved the id into the code block context
Maya (Eng): I reproduced locally. When a code fence is unclosed earlier on the page, docusaurus/mkdocs slugifier sometimes attaches heading IDs to the wrong element. Our parser upgrade tightened markdown rules so some previously-tolerant pages now render differently
Tara (Tech Writer): Quick fix: add explicit id on the heading to stabilize the anchor and fix the PR that introduced the stray backtick in the code sample. I'll open a tiny docs PR to both add the id and correct the code fence.
Felix (DevEx): Also add a small linkcheck exception for that fragment during the roll-out (so other unrelated PRs aren't blocked). We'll make it warning-only for 24h then require fix.
Maya (Eng): Patch for heading I'll push:
```md
## Sidebar collapse: when codefence breaks {#sidebar-collapse}
```
Tara (Tech Writer): Fixing the code fence around the example (missing closing ```):
```md
```bash
# deploy example
redwood deploy --region us-west-2
```
```
Jordan (Docs): PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/6122 (adds id + codefence fix + CI warning tweak)
DocBot: PR 6122 | checks started
Maya (Eng): After the fix, I also ran a grep for pages that contain "codefence" in the heading text and for pages with lone triple-backticks without a language tag; opened a couple more tiny PRs to close fences. This should reduce future flakiness
Felix (DevEx): I'll adjust linkcheck to treat known temporary exceptions as non-fatal and surface a nightly/email summary of remaining exceptions so we don't accidentally leave them forever
Jordan (Docs): Once CI green, we'll merge and deploy. Also adding a note to docs/contrib/markdown-linting.md: "Always close fenced code blocks; use explicit heading ids for anchors you expect to be stable."
Tara (Tech Writer): Thanks all, will follow up with the migration blurb and check top inbound anchors tomorrow
